hints: Focus on how the shape around carbon changes, because bond angle is decided by electron pair geometry and hybridisation.
Recall the key angles: tetrahedral $sp^3$ carbon is about $109.5^\circ$, trigonal planar $sp^2$ carbon is about $120^\circ$, and linear $sp$ in $\text{CO}_2$ is $180^\circ$.
Check each reaction to see if carbon goes from planar to tetrahedral, that $120^\circ$ to $109.5^\circ$ change is the only decrease here.
walkthrough:
**Link bond angle to shape**

Think shape first, angle second. More electron pairs pushing apart means a different shape.

$$sp^3 \text{ tetrahedral} \approx 109.5^\circ, \quad sp^2 \text{ trigonal planar} \approx 120^\circ, \quad sp \text{ linear in } \text{CO}_2 = 180^\circ$$

**Work out what each reaction does**

A is elimination: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{Br}$ to $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$. C is dehydration: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ to $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$. Both go $sp^3$ to $sp^2$.

$$109.5^\circ \rightarrow 120^\circ \text{ (increase)}$$

**Check combustion and polymerisation**

B is combustion: $\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{CO}_2$, so $109.5^\circ$ to $180^\circ$. That is a big increase. D is addition polymerisation: $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}_2$ to $\text{(-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-)}_n$.

$$120^\circ \rightarrow 109.5^\circ \text{ (decrease)}$$

**Pick the decrease**

Only the change from double bond planar to single bond tetrahedral gets smaller. That matches polymerisation of ethene.

options.A: Incorrect. Ethanolic NaOH causes dehydrohalogenation (elimination) of bromoethane to ethene. Carbon changes from tetrahedral $sp^3$ ($109.5^\circ$) to trigonal planar $sp^2$ ($120^\circ$), so the angle increases.
options.B: Incorrect. Complete combustion converts $\text{CH}_4$ to $\text{CO}_2$. Carbon changes from tetrahedral ($109.5^\circ$) to linear ($180^\circ$), so the angle increases a lot.
options.C: Incorrect. Hot conc. $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ dehydrates ethanol to ethene. Like option A, carbon goes from $sp^3$ ($109.5^\circ$) to $sp^2$ ($120^\circ$), so the angle increases.
options.D: Correct. Polymerisation of ethene is addition across the $\text{C=C}$ double bond to give poly(ethene). Each carbon changes from trigonal planar $sp^2$ ($120^\circ$) to tetrahedral $sp^3$ ($109.5^\circ$), so the bond angle decreases.
